risks: A UTXO owned (owner_scheme 4) by the token's own covenant id is spendable by anyone (any input of the token unlocks it); KOB never creates such an output (informational).

Genesis contamination: the covenant id commits only to the P2SH hashes of the genesis outputs, so a genesis may hide a non-template output able to mint look-alike tokens or feed a fake balance into a transfer; a token is verified only after every genesis output was checked (registry genesis record), until then it carries the warning genesis-unchecked.

risks: The is_minter path lets a live minter mint without limit: capability mint-authority.

Missing hardening present in kron-2732: does not refuse an all-zero owner on id_type 2 and does not refuse out-of-range output id types; the KOB orders never create such outputs (a plain UTXO carrying an order script fails the order's covenant-count check).

KRON id_type 3 (address presence) balances, the type KOB delivers to makers, are authorised by any P2PK input of the owner key: a maker signature with a partial sighash (SINGLE, NONE, ANYONECANPAY) would authorise all of that key's type-3 balances. KOB signers use SIGHASH_ALL only.

Genesis contamination: the covenant id commits only to the P2SH hashes of the genesis outputs, so a genesis may hide a non-template output able to mint look-alike tokens or feed a fake balance into a transfer; a token is verified only after every genesis output was checked (registry genesis record), until then it carries the warning genesis-unchecked.

Reviewed with conditions (internal review 2026-09-30, not an independent audit): a token is listed or official only after verify_genesis passes on its real genesis group and no live is_minter cell exists (its genesis record; a genesis without a minter output proves none can appear; a token with a live minter lists only with an active-mint-authority warning). Checked at review: order genesis groups are the order output alone, IOC returns are positional, x402 treats the token as issuer-controlled.

set_public_mint_active admits other covenant inputs and outputs that it does not account for (finding K-1, engine PoC review_b2_kaspacom r_kc_05..07): the creator of a mint_policy 2 token with a live minter lane spends the minter with one transfer_delegator holder cell (his own or a co-signer's) and writes one unchecked token-covenant output: a holder cell of any amount beyond max_supply, or a non-program UTXO carrying the token's covenant id that mints at will later.

K-1 limits and listing condition: other holders' balances and KOB scheme-4 escrows cannot be drawn in without their owner or order covenant; mint_policy 0 or 1 tokens and lanes with remaining_supply 0 are not affected. The backdoor appears after genesis, so the genesis check cannot see it. Minter lanes sit behind the extension commitment (G-2): a token lists only after a manual read of its minter extension shows policy 0 or 1, or every policy-2 lane exhausted.

source.note: Third-party KCC-20-compatible program (112-byte state, draft transfer tags, owner scheme 4 accepted). Pre-audit notes (adapter study): mint authority and the public-mint switch act on minter UTXOs (but see finding K-1 in risks), burn is authorised by the holder (an order authorises it only for its own pinned remainder), no freeze or seize entry. 25.5 KB program (about 5x the fee per fill of the reference), 8 in / 8 out, mass-bounded sweeps. Unmodified KOB orders custody and fill it (crates/kob-tests/tests/kob_kaspacom_tests.rs).

risks: A UTXO owned (owner_scheme 4) by the token's own covenant id is spendable by anyone (any input of the token unlocks it); KOB never creates such an output (informational).

Genesis contamination: the covenant id commits only to the P2SH hashes of the genesis outputs, so a genesis may hide a non-template output able to mint look-alike tokens or feed a fake balance into a transfer; a token is verified only after every genesis output was checked (registry genesis record), until then it carries the warning genesis-unchecked.

Issuance lives beside the program: the KCC20PublicMint app puts PublicMint minters (anyone mints up to their remaining allowance) and TokenSeed seeds (zero-amount holders) in the token's covenant id. kob registry verify-genesis accepts genesis minters and seeds of the published programs and records their allowance (genesis.mint_allowance): max supply = supply + mint_allowance, fixed at genesis. A token with a genesis minter is official only once no live minter has allowance left.

source.note: The build upstream publishes. Its state is the compiler-owned context gen__kcc20_template (the program's own Sil template hash 9703112e..., constant in every UTXO) followed by the standard 112-byte KCC20State; the template KOB pins is the KCC-1 actor-type handle of upstream's artifact (prefix = the 1-byte Sil prefix plus the context push, 34 B; suffix 3,885 B), so the unmodified KOB orders custody and fill it like every other 112-byte KCC-20 program. Every holder checks that the leader of its transfer is a KCC20 of this template; 3 token inputs / 3 token outputs per transfer.
